_note: Narration script for the AO amputation and haemorrhage module (CPP-042-AO v4.0, CPPRO-004). Lee voice on eleven_v4, [calmly] prefix, short conversational sentences, recorded as two takes (scenes 1 to 4, then 5 to 8). The prompt spells EOC and PCR as letters; captions use the text here.

lines.head: Introduction
sentences: Amputation and haemorrhage.
What every Ambulance Officer needs to know.

lines.head: Pressure first
sentences: Most bleeding stops with direct pressure.
Press firmly, and elevate the limb.
Start with basic care.
Consider clinical support, the EOC Clinician, and pain relief.

lines.head: A last resort
sentences: Life-threatening bleeding that pressure can't control?
Then, and only then, an arterial tourniquet.
It's a last resort.

lines.head: Where it goes
sentences: Put it on the limb, close to the wound, on the body side of it.
Never over a joint.
Never over the wound.

lines.head: Tighten and time
sentences: Tighten it until the bleeding is controlled, and you can't feel a pulse below it.
Lock the windlass.
Write the time on the strap, and on the PCR.

lines.head: Leave it on
sentences: Don't cover it.
Don't take it off.
And tell the EOC Clinician. They may get specialist advice.

lines.head: The amputated part
sentences: A complete amputation?
Seal the part in a water-tight bag.
Put the bag in ice-cooled water.
But never let the part touch the ice.

lines.head: Wrap-up
sentences: So. Press first. Tourniquet as a last resort.
Time it, leave it, tell them.
And keep the part off the ice.
Now, try the bleeding checker on this page.
